LESSON: WRITING 5.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING - PLAYS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.3: Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing - Plays
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing - Plays, part of Strand 5 in Grade 9 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How does a play differ from a story? 2. How are plays written?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. watch a live or recorded grade-appropriate skit in class and discuss the characters and use of dialogue,

2. search online or offline for grade- appropriate short play scripts related to the theme and read with peers,

3. work jointly with peers to discuss the features of a play with an emphasis on the characters, setting language, and stage directions,

4. sketch a one-scene play related to the theme,

5. exchange the play with peers for review,

6. revise the script according to the suggestions given by their peers,

7. write a two-scene play based on the theme,

8. work with peers to allocate roles and act out the play,

9. partner with peers to organise a class mini-festival and stage the plays, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. watch a live or recorded grade-appropriate skit in class and discuss the characters and use of dialogue,
2. search online or offline for grade- appropriate short play scripts related to the theme and read with peers,
3. work jointly with peers to discuss the features of a play with an emphasis on the characters, setting language, and stage directions,
4. sketch a one-scene play related to the theme,
5. exchange the play with peers for review,
6. revise the script according to the suggestions given by their peers,
7. write a two-scene play based on the theme,
8. work with peers to allocate roles and act out the play,
9. partner with peers to organise a class mini-festival and stage the plays, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing - Plays together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and imagination: The learner exchanges new ideas to inspire creativity when writing a two-scene play based on

the theme.

• Learning to learn: is enhanced as the learner plans and manages tasks effectively when partnering with peers to organise a

class mini-festival and stage the plays.

Values:
• Peace: This is enhanced as the learner displays tolerance with peers when organising a class mini-festival and staging the

plays.

• Social Justice: The learner accords equal opportunities when allocating roles to peers and acting out the play.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Ethnic Relations: This is promoted as the learner scripts and stages a creatively written play on the theme of cultural heritage.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of playwriting and cultural heritage to their learning of creative composition of artistic work

in Creative Arts and Sports.
